utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: I refuse to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it because you know that there's a pending investigation regarding the killing of Milan Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: I also don't want to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's because your involvement in that, that was an illegal killing, a war crime, was it not?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: Summon me to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, this line of questioning may prompt me to give the witness the warning under Rule 90. Witness, I want you to bear in mind that in these proceedings you are not obliged to answer any question that you think may incriminate you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need for me to answer such questions and I don't want to. I'm here to answer the questions that have to do with why I came here. He should ask that. I have enough arguments to keep on going for three days about the things he had done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it's because the stuff you don't want to talk about involves the death of civilian Serbs, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: There was only one civilian Serb who was killed around 40 years of age, and I doubt whether he was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour. I'm almost finished. A moment to confer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that there's a pending investigation in the Republika Srpska involving ten civilians that were killed and burned on August 1st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just ask -- investigations usually aren't public -- isn't usually a publicly known fact. Is this a publicly known fact that the witness could even know about, or is it something that's a confidential investigation or formerly confidential investigation that Mr. Alarid has information about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And my information is that I don't know the answer to Mr. Groome's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, do you have anything? You have nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No questions. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm a little bit hampered by the lack of the LiveNote, so I'm paraphrasing transcript but I'll give transcript references. Mr. Vilic, in response to a question that Judge Robinson asked, and this is at transcript 58, line 11, I believe the quote that you said was: "That was done by the Uzice Corps and White Eagles, that Milan Lukic did not do that and that he never had any unit of his." When you are using the word "that" in that context, what were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: I was told that by his lawyer. They said that I should state that. However, the fact is that Milan Lukic had his unit called Osvetnici.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But what is the thing that -- you say: "Milan did not do that." What did you understand being -- you were being told to say that Milan Lukic did not do?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: The attorneys asked me to provide such a statement. However, Milan Lukic did have a unit, and the Uzice and Valjevo Corps did not busy themselves with killing civilians. Once the Uzice Corps left, that's when the killings of civilians, women and children began.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The next question to you is, when was the first time someone raised the possibility that you might receive a benefit from giving testimony as a Defence witness for Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: MLD-10's husband said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you have recounted several conversations with him. When -- in which conversation was that matter first raised, or that possibility first raised?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: He mentioned it in the first and in the second, and actually in the third conversation that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to identify all of the people who raised with you the possibility that you might receive a benefit from your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: MLD-10's husband, MLD-10 herself, and allegedly Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alarid at page 44, line 13, of the transcript, put it to you that you were not in Bikavac area, but you were in the area of Kopito at the -- in the period of time in June. Can I ask you to tell us when you moved to Bikavac, and when you left Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: I arrived in Bikavac with my wife and children to my brother's house in the period between the 5th and the 8th of June, 1992. I was there in hiding for about ten days, in the forests outside Bikavac, and in the end I had to go through the forest at night to cross over to the free territory that was held by Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And during that ten-day period you were in Bikavac, did you ever go any further from where your brother was living apart from the woods that you described?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, just a minute. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that this examination is not something which is raised from the cross-examination, and I think that we are losing time in that examination. Thank you. THE COURT: We agree. Mr. Groome, it's going too far.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just one other question, Your Honour, if Your Honours permit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, not along the same lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, in cross-examination Mr. Alarid brought out that he saw Milan Lukic in Bikavac. I'm simply going to ask him does he recall when that was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Page 50, line 25, in response to a question by Mr. Alarid, you say that you saw Milan Lukic in Bikavac and that you were 5 metres away from him. Can you approximate when that was that you saw him in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA VILIC
utterances.text: Approximately on the 10th or 11th of July. June. June.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. That concludes your evidence. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes the Prosecution's presentation of its evidence in its case in chief against Milan and Sredoje Luke. We now rest our case conditionally in the light of three pending applications which I will state for the record at this time. One, there's a pending bar table motion for 65 ter 167. The motion is Prosecution's request for admission of Exhibit 65 ter 167 with confidential annexes A, B, C, and D. The second pending bar table motion is for 65 ter number 190.1 through 190.6. Prosecution's request for admission of Exhibits 65 ter 190.1 through 190.6. And finally, there's a pending matter with respect to the Chamber's decision on Mr. Amor Masovic's statement of the 4th of September, 2008. That's Exhibit P183 and related testimony. So the rest of -- I rest now the Prosecution's case conditioned upon whatever the Chamber decides when it resolves those three pending motions. That if the Chamber does grant our application to admit them as exhibits in our case in chief, that that so be done. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm to say that those decisions will be given shortly. Mr. Alarid, in accordance with the timetable that we had set, I believe we had indicated that following the end of the Prosecution's case we will --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was saying that in accordance with the timetable that had been set, we had indicated that following the end of the Prosecution's case, we would hear the submissions on 98 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And I was assuming -- actually what I had heard last week, although I heard something different right when we closed evidence on Thursday, is that is what I heard is that we would start right after. But I believe that earlier the schedule was last witness today, 98 bis tomorrow, and then ruling by the Court presumably maybe Thursday. And then as we were going through kind of the issues of the case, this weekend discussing that, that was one of the things that came up amongst us procedurally was with pending motions outstanding. I mean, the nuance might not be much considering the issues that are there, but I think we do need the Court's rulings on those motions before we make a final submission as this course, you know, Amor Masovic being, I think, a bright line may impact the argument for 98 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: They will not. Are you in a position to begin your submissions now, or are you asking for --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm asking for tomorrow. I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a pleasure to inform this honourable Trial Chamber that our Defence team will not raise 98 bis submission. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll hear you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I just ask one thing, I note that a new colleague has joined Mr. Alarid. Maybe he would do us the courtesy in introducing the new attorney on the case to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a legal assistant. Intern, I mean. Christopher Lyerla. No new attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of November 2008, at 3.45 p.m.
